title: Optional Module A: Comparison of Traditional Media with Electronic Media
summary: Every medium has its own strengths and weaknesses and is useful in different situations; radio and television did not end newspapers and traditional media. Because of familiar format, content and local language, traditional media have clarity; their greatest advantage over electronic media is flexibility in accommodating new themes (comments on current events in the tamasha and jatra).

Advantages of traditional media: most useful in human communication; no special training or technology; embedded in one's culture and tradition; feedback is immediate and known; flexible in changing form and content for the context (songs for a social cause without changing the form); cost effective; easy to remember and attract the masses; intimate with the masses in all regions; primary appeal is to emotions rather than intellect; an immense variety of forms and themes; local and live, with direct rapport with the audience; easily available; enjoyed by all age groups. Advantages of electronic media: large outreach with heterogeneous audiences; messages communicated within no time to many people at a time; variety of audio, video and text in one medium; recording and archiving; live programmes make distance no hindrance; possibly interactive. Disadvantages of traditional media: restricted to the place of performance, limited reach and audience, limited scope for archiving. Disadvantages of electronic media: less intimate, slow feedback, expensive, special training required to make programmes, limited access in rural areas.
## Nature of traditional and electronic media

Traditional media (an informal and unscripted medium) is most appropriate for changing attitudes and helping rural masses accept social change (cleanliness); it is most effective in rural and tribal areas and among illiterates; it expresses socio-cultural, religious, moral and emotional needs and conveys educational messages through entertainment, colour, costume, music and dance. It also sustains agriculture: demonstrations (story telling and plays at weekly markets to encourage new ideas), fairs (awareness of improved technology in a lively informal atmosphere), interaction with experts (visits to farms and research organisations) and puppetry (combines entertainment with education), all used face to face. Electronic media (radio and television) use sight and hearing; radio stimulates imagination and is portable and low cost; television has audio-visual power; they have immediacy and timeliness, huge dissemination capacity and cover vast areas economically, but television has changed living habits and values and can affect children's behaviour.

Myths about traditional media: that they have no relevance now and are not effective. Though they cater to small audiences, the impact is deeper and audiences participate; they preserve culture; they are often more effective for development messages.
## Integration of traditional and electronic media

Traditional media forms are used for messages on agriculture, primary health care, nutrition, education and women and child rights, live and integrated with electronic media. Electronic media extend the coverage of a traditional performance, while traditional media enrich electronic channels with colour, costume, dance and music. Traditional media should be an integral part of communication programmes for rural development. Prerequisites: understanding of the rural audience and entertainment to attract attention. Points of consideration: retain social authenticity; choose the most suitable form (the Maharashtra tamasha cannot be used effectively for social messages in rural Kerala); keep the original form (adaptation should not alter or destroy it); collaboration between folk artists and producers is essential; electronic media will not completely replace traditional media, just as television did not end newspaper reading.

objA: State true or false: (i) Traditional media has limited scope for archiving the performance. (ii) Traditional media has an immense variety of forms and themes to suit the communication requirements of the masses.

State true or false: (i) Demonstrations are a useful tool for imparting education through classroom teaching and learning in educational institutions. (ii) Puppetry combines entertainment and education for communicating awareness on social issues.
Match: (a) Demonstration (b) Puppetry with (i) Encourages farmers to try new ideas (ii) Combines entertainment with education.
State true or false: (i) Traditional media is culture-specific. (ii) It needs advanced technology.
Fill in the blanks: Traditional media are most effective in ______, ______ areas and among ______.
State true or false: (i) Electronic media have slow feedback mechanisms. (ii) Traditional media are expensive compared to electronic media.
Fill in the blanks: Integration of traditional media with electronic media should retain the ______ of the traditional form.
Name any two advantages of electronic media.
Wide outreach; messages in no time to many people; recording and archiving (any two).
vsaA: Mention any two advantages of traditional media.
They are cost effective and flexible to accommodate new themes; also local, live, with immediate feedback and need no special training.
Why do we consider 'flexibility' as one of the important factors of traditional media?
Because their form and content can be changed for the context and new themes, e.g. songs on a social cause or comments on current events in tamasha.
What should be done while integrating traditional media with electronic media for development purposes? Write any two points of consideration.
Retain the social authenticity and original form of the traditional media; choose a suitable form for the region; keep collaboration between folk artists and producers.
Identify any two uses of traditional media in society. Give suitable examples.
Creating awareness on social issues such as polio immunisation through puppetry, and educating farmers through demonstrations and fairs.
List any two disadvantages of electronic media.
They are expensive and less intimate; feedback is slow; special training is required.
What are the myths about traditional media?
That they have no relevance in the present context and are not effective for communication.
laA: Write down any four advantages of traditional media that distinguish them from electronic media. Give examples.
Local and live with direct rapport (street play); flexible to new themes (tamasha); cost effective and need no special training (folk songs); immediate known feedback and emotional appeal.
Discuss the relevance of traditional media in modern society.

They reach rural and tribal people and illiterates, are flexible and cheap, preserve culture, give deeper impact through audience participation and are being integrated with electronic media for development messages.
Compare traditional media with electronic media.

Traditional media are local, live, intimate, flexible and cost effective but limited in reach and archiving; electronic media reach large heterogeneous audiences instantly with recording but are expensive, less intimate and slow in feedback.
